content.text:
Short answer: there isn’t one “best” clinic for everyone, but these are the most reliable places in Singapore. Pick based on surgeon, procedure options (LASIK vs SMILE vs TransPRK/PRK), price transparency and your eye profile.

- Singapore National Eye Centre (SNEC) – Laser Vision Centre
  - National specialty eye hospital; offers the full suite (Femto-LASIK, SMILE pro, TransPRK/ASA, LASEK, ICL). Transparent fees and strong audit culture. As of Aug 1, 2025, bladeless LASIK is S$1,940–S$2,049 per eye (incl. 9% GST) and includes 1-year enhancement if needed. ([snec.com.sg](https://www.snec.com.sg/our-specialties/clinical-interests/refractive-surgery/lasik))

- Clearvision Eye Clinic & LASIK Centre
  - Private clinic known for flapless options (TransPRK/“no-touch”) plus SMILE and femto-LASIK. Publishes all‑inclusive prices: TransPRK S$4,588 both eyes; SMILE pro 2.0 S$5,388; Femto‑LASIK S$4,588 (incl. GST, surgery/facility/meds/first follow‑ups). ([clearvision.com.sg](https://clearvision.com.sg/prices/))

- LSC Eye Clinic (Paragon)
  - Formerly “The LASIK Surgery Clinic” (est. 2005). Offers ZEISS SMILE pro, LASIK, TransPRK/PRK, LASIK Xtra and ICL; convenient Orchard location. ([lsceye.sg](https://lsceye.sg/?gad_source=1))

- Atlas Eye Specialist Centre (Paragon and Royal Square @ Novena)
  - Private subspecialist centre offering PRK, wavefront bladeless LASIK and ReLEx SMILE with detailed pre‑/post‑op guidance. Two central locations. ([atlaseye.sg](https://atlaseye.sg/))

- Eagle Eye Centre
  - Large multi‑subspecialty private group; provides LASIK and TransPRK with modern laser platforms (e.g., Wavelight Allegretto and Ziemer femto for bladeless LASIK). Multiple sites. ([eagleeyecentre.com.sg](https://eagleeyecentre.com.sg/?utm_source=openai))

- Shinagawa Eye Centre (Orchard)
  - Long‑established Orchard clinic providing LASIK and comprehensive eye screening; widely used by insurers and corporates. ([shinagawa.com.sg](https://www.shinagawa.com.sg/services/lasik?utm_source=openai))

Costs at a glance (mid‑2025/2026)
- Public route (SNEC): about S$3.9k–S$4.1k for both eyes for bladeless LASIK, plus consults/meds. ([snec.com.sg](https://www.snec.com.sg/our-specialties/clinical-interests/refractive-surgery/lasik))
- Private route: packages commonly S$4.6k–S$5.4k for both eyes depending on procedure/clinic. Example: Clearvision TransPRK S$4,588; SMILE S$5,388. ([clearvision.com.sg](https://clearvision.com.sg/prices/))
- Note on payment: LASIK is considered cosmetic; no subsidy and MediSave cannot be used. ([snec.com.sg](https://www.snec.com.sg/our-specialties/clinical-interests/refractive-surgery/faqs?utm_source=openai))

How to choose quickly
- Surgeon and scope: favour clinics where refractive surgeons perform all major options (LASIK, SMILE, TransPRK/PRK, ICL) so the recommendation fits your cornea and lifestyle, not just one machine. SNEC, LSC, Atlas, Eagle Eye and Clearvision all offer multiple options. ([snec.com.sg](https://www.snec.com.sg/our-specialties/clinical-interests/refractive-surgery/what-we-do?utm_source=openai))
- Technology and diagnostics: ask which femtosecond/excimer platforms and topography/aberrometry they use, and about enhancement policies and dry‑eye management. (SNEC and Eagle Eye list their platforms publicly.) ([snec.com.sg](https://www.snec.com.sg/our-specialties/clinical-interests/refractive-surgery/lasik))
- Price transparency: confirm what fees include (meds, first‑month follow‑ups, enhancements). SNEC and Clearvision publish details. ([snec.com.sg](https://www.snec.com.sg/our-specialties/clinical-interests/refractive-surgery/lasik))
- Setting: public hospital (SNEC) can be cost‑efficient with academic oversight; private clinics often offer shorter wait times and surgeon continuity.

If you want me to narrow it to 2–3 specific clinics, tell me:
- Your age and prescription (approx. power/astigmatism) and whether it’s stable
- Dry eye history or contact lens intolerance
- Sports or military/LEO needs (may favour flapless options)
- Budget and preference for public vs private

Practical next steps
- Book 1–2 suitability assessments to compare opinions. Expect 2–3 hours of tests. Stop soft contacts for at least 3 days before the evaluation (14 days if wearing hard/RGP lenses); individual clinics may advise longer. ([atlaseye.sg](https://atlaseye.sg/your-pre-lasik-evaluation-process-at-atlas-eye-specialist-centre/?utm_source=openai))
- If you proceed, similar contact‑lens stop rules apply before surgery; your clinic will confirm specifics. ([atlaseye.sg](https://atlaseye.sg/treatments/refractive-surgery/laser-vision-correction/before-surgery/?utm_source=openai))
